steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: Over here!

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: Surround her, don't let her through!

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: Attention all forces! Get ready!
The feeling of weightlessness returns.
Calcium crystals grow rapidly, tethering Saria's hand to the corridor floor.

steps.name: Components Control Section Employee
steps.text: The second 'Disorder' wave is starting!

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: ...Disorder?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Nasti's magnum opus.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You've been following me around for the last couple of days. Does Defense have nothing else to do?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Sixteen of your Rhine Technological Park modifications do not comply with our established safety regulations.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: (Speaks in Sarkaz) Disorder.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Abandon the sense of balance inside your mind. Instead of fighting the chaos, try adapting to its rhythm instead.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Find what you've been looking for?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You reconfigured several key structures in the park. You don't seem to be following any rules, but... the connections between the components make sense.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I could have never imagined that structures like these would be possible.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: A linear language constricts most people's imagination.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: If you have a specific future in mind, you must first construct a dialogue with the destination, instead of brute-forcing a route.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Abandon... balance.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Perceive the destination...
She frees up both her hands.
The next shift in gravity comes abruptly, and as she hits the ceiling, she takes the opportunity to maneuver her trajectory, and jumps over the soldiers hot on her tail.
Calcium crystals follow in her wake, drawing an arc.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Manipulating raw calcium in the same way microbes change their composition... how very enlightening.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: The materials morph extremely quickly, are adaptable and combinable with various organs, and thus have promising medical applications.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: This has been your research field ever since you were in college, yes? Why not continue?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Because it's dangerous.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Are you referring to the ethical issues arising from the construction of artificial organs with this technique?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: More than that.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Giving new techniques to doctors may save lives; but if they fall into the hands of criminals, they could also be reduced to weapons of destruction.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Haha. I almost forgot how rich with calcium our bodies are.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Therefore, I have determined that my research in this field must be suspended until effective control measures have been established.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: It's a terrible pity, you know that?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: If you ever change your mind, Rhine Lab could certainly have two sections specializing in life sciences.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Rhine Lab needs a Defense Section more.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'm giving you my data in the hopes that you can combine our experiences to better evaluate the risks of the chimeric experiments.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Don't go too far, Parvis. The cost of pushing our boundaries will be too high for us all.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Then, where does the boundary lie?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Countless studies have shown that the evolution of life has not been a gradual process, contrary to the theories of the earliest scholars in this field. We wouldn't be standing here right now if we had only been taking one step at a time.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Furthermore, if we presume that there is indeed a boundary drawn by a higher will, that determines how we should be acting—

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Shouldn't we try to look it in the eye first, before we decide to kneel or raise a flag of rebellion?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: ...A 'boundary'. This corridor... is also a boundary.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: If I keep walking along the corridor... I'll never reach wherever the 'eye' is.
The 'H.A.M.H.R.R.'
This ring-shaped laboratory has from its inception, been designed to subvert people's perceptions.
It is the realization of Kristen's dreams, the real product of Rhine Lab's Components Control Section, the combined wisdom of practically every Rhine Lab Director.
Saria is familiar with how each of them operate, but in the past, she had not allowed herself to think in the same way.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: This makes no sense... No, it doesn't matter.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I have long been disgusted with this wall.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The telescope we borrowed from the Stargazers Association broke down.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Don't worry about it. The view here is great, you can see many stars with just the naked eye.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Well, you go look for a nice place to sit down. I'll try fixing it.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Wow... O great superhuman Lady Saria, I'm sooo curious, is there honestly anything you can't do?

spans.text: Wow... O great superhuman Lady Saria, I'm sooo curious, is there honestly anything you

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I recommend you check my personal course electives. I won't be able to do anything I'm not studying.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You're a terrifying studying machine!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Whoa, it's so cold today... want a candy? Cream puffs? Hot chocolate?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Consuming sweets this late at night is not conducive to good health.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Booooring.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Kristen, look at that rock, what do you think it looks like?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oh, come on! It looks like Saria, right? It's so hard, and yet it shines so 'perfectly!'

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: ...Like the stars.
Kristen grabs the shining stone, and looks up.
She seems to be comparing it to something, as she moves the rock around.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Something's wrong. There should be a star here, but there isn't one.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I've done so many calculations... and yet I haven't figured out the trajectory of the stars.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You've already failed so many times, you still believe it's measurable?

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Hm... I prefer to say that I 'don't believe.'

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I don't believe in all the rules I've been taught. I don't believe that humanity will never be able to pierce through the starpod, let alone believe that the stars are only as small as we see them.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: There's no way you believe we can fly all the way to the stars, right? I thought only a kid would believe stuff like that!

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Children, poets, and scientists.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Haha, who ever said I wasn't one?

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Scientists do not believe that dreams are false. Because what they're essentially doing is proving to all humanity that dreams can come true.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Gosh, you really have a one track mind.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So, Kristen. When our Rhine Lab becomes a full fledged public company, are we gonna keep that Lab on the name, or change it to Rhine Something Else?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'm studying ecology, and Saria's research is in bioengineering and microorganisms, so the two of us are down to keep it nice and generic. Two against one, us in the life sciences... Just kidding.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I mean, you're dead set on soaring through the skies, and your field is high-energy physics, so wouldn't you wanna call it 'Rhine Physics' instead?

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: We'll stick with 'Rhine Lab.' It's a good name.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I want to know exactly what the stars we're looking at are.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I want to know what's outside the barrier encasing around us.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I want to know... if we really manage to walk among the stars, and look back from over there, what kind of land we've actually been living on.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: All the questions I seek have mostly to do with not just me, but 'we.'

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: And 'we'... we are all beings trapped in this teeny tiny corner.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: How are you planning to compensate me for breaking my vivarium, Saria?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You knew Kristen's plans from the very beginning.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Are you talking about 'Arc-01'... or 'Galleria Stellaria'?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: 'Arc-01' was never more than a front to deceive the military, a pile of scrap paper that was never feasible.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: 'Galleria Stellaria' is the real laboratory here, or you could also say, the name of this aircraft.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Heh... it certainly is a name that she would come up with.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Yup, the only thing she thinks about.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: So you replicated your vivarium up here. Is Kristen intending to break through the barrier with it?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Just tearing the 'starpod' open won't be enough for her, you know.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Without a doubt.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Her fixation was never the barrier, but the realm beyond that even our ancestors have yet to reach.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: She truly wants to step inside that deep outer space. She wants to leave everything that can be left behind in that dimension.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And that includes...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Each and every life present in this vivarium.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: As soon as I heard about the 'Galleria Stellaria' project, I started gathering a variety of plant species that might be able to survive in the environment outside the barrier.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I just checked, and there's seven hundred and fifty-three different types here. Kristen put them all in this lab.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'm pretty happy about it... we'll be able to find our answer together real soon.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You want to know if life can exist among the stars.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And especially... yourself.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: ...Yup.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: My people and I... we've been trapped in this cage that just continues to shrink.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: As time goes by, we can only follow what happens to water that can't be contained, wind that dissipates, trees that wither, and vanish from this ever changing land.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: And then, she said to me...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: 'Then, let's go.'

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: 'This land is not your home, but beyond it... there might just be a space untainted by Originium that will really accept you and your people.'

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: A mere hypothesis.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: So far, no instrument has managed to penetrate, or even approach the barrier. So there is no basis to assert the possibility of Originium's absence beyond the barrier, let alone the total lack of evidence to suggest that life can survive in the depths of outer space.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's just a dream. There's no evidence or data to support it, and it goes against all the scientific knowledge I have.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But... Scientists don't believe that dreams are false. Because what they're essentially doing is proving to all humanity that dreams can come true.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I remember Kristen said that.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Yes. She's the same as ever.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: What about us?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Saria...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Have we... changed at all?
Water spreads out like hands in all directions, pinning Saria to the wall.
Saria has never seen water this fierce out of Muelsyse. It is like a waterfall, like a tsunami, as if the water is howling.
Calcium crystals continuously grow from Saria's hands, but they fail to take form under the sweeping waves.
She tries to find Muelsyse, but all she finds in stream after stream of water are the eyes of an elf hidden in the depths of each wave.
Eyes filled with serenity and grief.
The water is howling, but the elf is crying.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I really... really wish, we could be together forever, just like on that starlit night.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But there's no way I can hold onto the both of you at the same time.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Dancing in threes... really is too hard.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Ugh... Ggh...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I won't give you a chance to stop her.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Because... haha, two against one. This time, I'm on her side.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Muel...syse...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sleep, Saria. Go to sleep.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You're all black and blue and probably about to pass out. There's no need for you to keep fighting, because our dreams are about to come true.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So just close your eyes and the water will take you away from here. By the time you wake up, Kristen and I will have reached our destination.
A solid calcium crystal does not stab at the water in vain, but into the side of the bulkhead.
Saria is well aware that the next 'disorder' is about to happen.

steps.name: Robotic Voice
steps.text: Warning—

steps.name: Robotic Voice
steps.text: Energy overload initiated. All secondary compartmental gravity systems and dampers have failed.

steps.name: Robotic Voice
steps.text: Attention all personnel, energy overload initiated—

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Eek?!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Why... would it suddenly...?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Sudden? No.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You were right, Kristen has never changed.
The instantaneous gravitational shift causes the streams of water to lose direction.
The enamel piercing through the bulkhead firmly fixes Saria on the spot, but Muelsyse is tossed outside along with her water.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Saria!

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You're the same as ever. Whenever you get nervous, you forget just how fragile your body is.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Uhh... no, catch me! I don't want to leave... not alone...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The energy overload is starting.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: When it's done charging, the entire platform will collapse. Even if you can get close to, or even break through the barrier, the core cabin will not last long enough.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Kristen wants to save you.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: ...As do I.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Yes, I want to bring her back.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Muelsyse... after gravity returns to normal, leave this place.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: What happens next is between the two of us.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: ...Saria!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: No! I gotta hold onto something—!

steps.name: Robotic Voice
steps.text: Authentication—failed.

steps.name: Robotic Voice
steps.text: Your clearance has expired. Galleria Stellaria Vivarium—Access Denied.

steps.name: Robotic Voice
steps.text: Your clearance has expired. Galleria Stellaria Vivarium—Access Denied.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Saria! You dummy! Blockhead! Knucklehead! Open the door!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ha... haha...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I've really been... abandoned again.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Saria... I hope you make it...
Saria stands at the door leading to the deepest part of the lab, knowing her target is just inside.
However, before she can even condense the calcium crystals on her hand, the door lock automatically releases.
Compared to the previous area filled with instruments and equipment, this place feels more like a temple to the stars.
A sphere made of smooth and flawless metal shows off its dazzling beauty under the soft light.
Spheres of varying sizes slowly glide on predetermined orbits one after another, with their paths changing now and then.
The irregularities intertwine with each other, but contrary to expectations, they form an indescribable sense of harmony.
Whether it be the positions of the stars, or how precise their orbits shift, the planetarium exceeds the imaginations of any astrologer.
But in the very next moment, those devoted to the stars would probably fly into a rage.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Those so-called astrologers are basically misguided zealots.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: For the past thousand years, they've committed themselves to tracking the trajectory of the stars.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Every trajectory change that occurs signifies a new revelation, or a meaningful omen to them.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Their behavior is not necessarily incomprehensible.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: The fact that the stars move without a trace is enough to terrify most people.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: To believe that the stars are mere pawns of an undiscoverable being, that their movements and trajectory changes hold any meaning is obviously the more reassuring choice.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: However—
Kristen extends a hand toward the planetarium.
The dome of Galleria Stellaria enveloping the ceiling suddenly opens itself.
False starlight floods the laboratory.
Kristen makes a series of gestures with her hand, and in an instant, the planetarium completely transforms.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Fake.
The stars begin to move erratically.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: False.
Several stars collide with one another. Though they do not shatter, the sound of them crashing into each other instantly destroys the silence in the room.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Fabricated.
However, Kristen's expression does not change at all.
As if everything is as it should be.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: If the trajectories are really just invisible, then how have we avoided colliding with other stars throughout the last millennium?

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Are we so special to have avoided such a fate so far?

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: What kind of land have we actually been living on?

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Where exactly are we headed?

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: These questions... I've whispered them in your ears too many times to count.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Can you help me move that 'planet' over there, Saria?
A small metallic sphere passes by Saria's hand.
'Star.'
Instead of touching it, she lets it fall out of orbit.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: What a shame.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I've been fiddling with these planets before we break the barrier, and no matter how many times I try, they just refuse to stay on the right track.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: ...Stop this, Kristen.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: We still have time to turn back, before you hit the barrier with this Galleria Stellaria.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: 'Galleria Stellaria'... isn't it exactly as how I described it to you before?

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: A pity that you had already left Rhine Lab by the time I built it.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: But I knew you would come back. At the very moment when my dreams were about to be realized... you would be there.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Whether or not you're with me—

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: —Or against me.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: This time, it's my turn to make the first move.
Kristen lifts her hand, revealing the exoskeleton operating system Saria is most familiar with, and gently makes a fist.

Silver liquid spews out from the planetarium behind Kristen, and in an instant, all the planets are thrown out of their orbits, rushing towards a single position at a speed too fast for the naked eye.
The entire galaxy pours down on Saria.
